thesis: Provisional thesis: under synthetic workload conditions, a bounded adaptive checkpoint interval based on a rolling failure-hazard estimate can reduce expected recomputation relative to a fixed 30-minute baseline while respecting a ten-percent checkpoint-I/O budget.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.goal: Frame the checkpointing problem, the synthetic-study scope, and the need to evaluate adaptation together with prediction error and storage cost.

sections.title: Adaptive Policy and Evaluation Design
sections.goal: Specify the synthetic trace, fixed 30-minute baseline, bounded adaptive policy, rolling hazard estimate, and evaluation measures.

sections.title: Expected Recomputation, Sensitivity, and Storage Overhead
sections.goal: Compare the adaptive policy with the fixed baseline and separate expected recomputation, prediction-error sensitivity, and checkpoint-storage overhead.

sections.title: Limitations and Implications
sections.goal: Bound the interpretation to synthetic observations, discuss threats to validity, and exclude production or universal claims.

sections.title: Conclusion
sections.goal: Restate the constrained contribution and the evaluation principle without extending the evidence beyond the synthetic study.
